text:
anne-infra: Heads up — after the BMC firmware push last night a subset of eu-central racks (rack-eu1-[02,03,07]) are failing provisioning. OOB shows SecureBoot flag toggled to ENFORCED even though we didn't push signing keys. PXE boots get dropped mid-TFTP. :warning:
simon: Which firmware image did we push? Can you paste the BMC logs / ipmi output?
jess: Saw this pattern before — a metadata mismatch in the BMC image sets the UEFI attribute to 'lock' after a reboot. Quick check: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** sel list` and `ipmitool fru print` to confirm.
anne-infra: Image is rbw-bmc-v3.2.1 (rolling). Log excerpt from one host: `BMC: secure_boot_state=1, secure_keys_present=0, boot_order=network, tftp_err=timed_out`
matt-sre: ops-bot canary shows fail rate spiking from 0.6% -> 7.1% over the last 40 minutes in eu-central. Provisioner is auto-routing but we're saturating us-west spare pool.
ops-bot: alert: provisioner.coldstart.fail_rate[euc1] = 0.071 ; affected_nodes = 128 ; action = reroute_to_pool(us-west-spare)
katie-eng: Rerouting is fine short-term but note network egress and cross-region data transfer will add CPU and storage egress. Finance owner @finance-ops FYI — rough incremental cost if we keep 200 GPUs in us-west on-demand for 7 days?
finance-ops: Rough ballpark +$2.7k for 7 days if we shift 200 A100-equivalent to on-demand. If we use reserved spare capacity we can halve that.
simon: Before we escalate, can we attempt a BMC attribute flip over IPMI instead of mass rollback? Command I used previously (careful):
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.0.12.34 -U admin -P <redacted> raw 0x30 0x45 0x01 0x00
# toggles secure boot attr to 'clear' on some vendors — test on single node first
```
jess: YMMV across vendors. Some ASPEED/BMC combos ignore raw. We should not run blanket on the rack. Test on rack-eu1-02 first.
anne-infra: Testing note: I ran the ipmi raw flip on rack-eu1-02: node-024 recovered and provisioned cleanly. node-031 in same rack still stuck. Logs show `UEFI_VARIABLE_WRITE_ERROR`. Possibly NVRAM corruption on the board.
matt-sre: If it's NVRAM corruption we need per-host fallback: 1) attempt soft-clear of secure attr 2) if fails, mark host as 'manual-reprovision' and drain 3) allocate from fallback pool.
katie-eng: Also let's pause the v3.2.1 rollout immediately and revert the image from canary. deploy-bot: please start rollback.
deploy-bot: rollback: rbw-bmc-v3.2.1 -> rbw-bmc-v3.2.0 initiated by katie-eng at 2765440200 ; rolling pause set for eu-central ; will stop new pushes to same hardware.
ops-bot: Adding short-term autoscaling rule: increase us-west-spare pool by +40 instances (200 GPUs) with preemptible fallback disabled for latency-sensitive jobs.
finance-ops: Approving up to $3k emergency spend for cross-region capacity for next 72 hours. Please submit exact numbers to budget channel.
anne-infra: Action items: 1) Pause rollout (done). 2) Run IPMI flip test on rack-eu1-02 & 03 (simon + jess). 3) Triage nodes with UEFI_VARIABLE_WRITE_ERROR to manual reprovision (matt-sre). 4) Reroute provisioning to us-west-spare (ops-bot) and track cost (finance-ops). 5) Postmortem to include why secure_keys_present==0 after rollout (katie-eng).
simon: Working on test now — will update within 15m. :eyes:
jess: I'll coordinate the vendor support request for NVRAM write failures; might need board RMA for ~12 nodes.
matt-sre: I'll script a safe drain + taint so scheduler won't send jobs to partially-provisioned nodes: `rbctl drain --reason "bmc-secboot-uefi" --nodes node-031,node-045`
anne-infra: Thanks. Keep threads short updates only — escalate to incidents channel if we hit >15% fail rate or >500 GPUs rerouted.
katie-eng: After this stabilizes we should add a preflight check for secure_keys_present in the rollout CI — prevent the image from setting ENFORCED if keys absent.
finance-ops: I'll follow up with exact numbers for the budget channel.
ops-bot: monitoring: reroute_in_progress(us-west-spare) ; current_rerouted_gpus=164 ; expected_peak_spend_rate=$420/day
